title: Wheelchair Pick-and-Roll Reads
description: A ball handler and a screener run a chair screen, with the ball handler reading the defenders' positions to decide between attacking downhill and finding the screener rolling to the rim.

content.objective: Set a legal, stationary chair screen and read the defense to choose between attacking downhill or finding the roll.
content.setup: A ball handler and screener run a side screen at the top of the key against two live defenders.
instructions: The screener gets fully stationary before the ball handler uses the screen — a moving chair screen is a foul.
The ball handler reads whether the screener's defender helps or stays attached.
If the defender helps off the screener, the screener rolls hard to the rim for the pass.
If the defender stays attached, the ball handler attacks downhill off the screen instead.
coachingPoints: The screener must be completely stopped and legally positioned before any contact.
Read the help defender's chair position, not just guess which option to take.
Attack downhill in a straight, direct line off a good screen — don't drift sideways.
commonMistakes: Screening while still moving, which is an illegal moving screen.
Ball handler going too wide around the screen and losing the advantage it created.
Cutting without actually drawing any real defensive attention.
content.safety: Screens must be fully stationary and legal; defenders should not initiate extra contact fighting through.
progressions: Add a second live defender rotation to simulate a full help-side read.
regressions: Walk through the screen angle and the two reads at a slow pace with no defense first.
